mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a fast pullback in discretionary trips; within four weeks that suppresses mall, dining, and shopping visits, pushing RETAIL_REC lower than the prior four-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -42.6 to -63.3 and TRANSIT from -44.6 to -49.9 in t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below their t-1w levels, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects people staying home more and replacing outside shopping with at-home activity, so retail and recreation falls further over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +20 and stays elevated for one week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7-14 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds +20, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall sharply at the same time, the city is experiencing a mobility constraint regime; that regime reduces incidental shopping trips and drives RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by at least 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to -49.9 and WORKPLACES to -63.3 in t-0w
failure_condition: If simultaneous week-on-week declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are followed by stable or rising RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A deep drop in PARKS mobility marks adverse weather or holiday displacement of outdoor leisure; when park use collapses, discretionary outing demand also falls, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -20.9 to -50.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after PARKS drops below -40, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC indicates broad trip suppression rather than substitution; this pattern should continue to depress retail visits over the next four weeks as households consolidate errands.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -8.3 to -24.1 while RETAIL_REC fell from -31.0 to -64.9 in t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains depressed but RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT after a sharp trough indicates restored access to commercial districts; once transit recovers, retail and recreation should rise with a lag of about four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 8 points from its prior week low
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -49.9 vs -44.6 one week earlier but remains depressed
failure_condition: If TRANSIT recovers by 8 points or more from a low but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall, a stay-at-home regime is active; that combination suppresses shopping trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stay below -40
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 25.0 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stayed very negative in t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 and WORKPLACES/TRANSIT remain below -40 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run stabilization in PARKS after a prior decline can precede a rebound in discretionary movement, and that rebound should lift retail visits within one week if people are reallocating outing time back to shopping.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stops falling and rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -24.1 to -22.1 to -20.9 before dropping to -50.4
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes or rises but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls in the next 7 days, the hypothesis fails.
